svg.title: Recovery paths geometry draft
svg.desc: Alternate A0 poster draft emphasizing encoder and readout geometry.

rect.style: stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

text.style: font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 700; font-size: 73px;fill: rgb(7%,14%,21%); stroke:none;

g.text: Multiple Recovery Paths in a Lesioned Transformer

text.style: font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 700; font-size: 51px;fill: rgb(7%,24%,40%); stroke:none;
font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 700; font-size: 29px;fill: rgb(7%,14%,21%); stroke:none;
font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px;fill: rgb(7%,24%,40%); stroke:none;
font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 700; font-size: 36px;fill: rgb(7%,24%,40%); stroke:none;
font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 400; font-size: 24px;fill: rgb(7%,14%,21%); stroke:none;

g.text: Using BERT as a frozen encoder and a linear part-of-speech (POS) readout as a task classifier, we first use gate masking

text.style: font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 400; font-size: 24px;fill: rgb(7%,14%,21%); stroke:none;

g.text: to learn a sparse core subnetwork sufficient for POS classification. We then ablate this subnetwork to produce a large

text.style: font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 400; font-size: 24px;fill: rgb(7%,14%,21%); stroke:none;

g.text: drop in performance. Our main question is whether performance can recover by adapting the surviving

text.style: font-family: 'Bitstream Vera Sans'; font-weight: 400; font-size: 24px;fill: rgb(7%,14%,21%); stroke:none;

g.text: projection-specific gates, retraining the linear POS readout, or both.
